questions.title: Design URL Shortener (like bit.ly)
questions.question:
Design a URL shortener service like bit.ly.

Requirements:
- Shorten long URLs to short codes (e.g., bit.ly/abc123)
- Redirect short URLs to original URLs
- 100M URLs stored, 10K writes/second, 100K reads/second
- Custom aliases (user-defined short codes)
- Analytics: click count, referrer, geographic location
- URL expiration support
- Global deployment, <100ms latency
- High availability (99.99%)

Design:
1. API design (shorten, redirect, analytics)
2. Short code generation algorithm
3. Database schema (SQL vs NoSQL)
4. Handling collision in short codes
5. Caching strategy for hot URLs
6. CDN usage for global distribution
7. Analytics storage and querying
8. Custom alias validation
9. URL expiration mechanism
10. Scalability (sharding, read replicas)
11. Capacity estimation (storage, bandwidth, QPS)
12. Monitoring and metrics
questions.realWorldScenario: Classic system design interview question with practical application

questions.title: Design Pastebin (like pastebin.com)
questions.question:
Design a text sharing service like Pastebin.

Requirements:
- Users paste text content, get shareable URL
- Support syntax highlighting for code
- Expiration options (10min, 1hr, 1day, 1week, never)
- Private/public/unlisted visibility
- Edit history for logged-in users
- 10M active users, 1M pastes/day
- Average paste size: 10KB, max 512KB
- Read-heavy (100:1 read:write ratio)
- Global availability

Design:
1. Database schema for pastes
2. Paste ID generation strategy
3. Storage solution (database vs object storage)
4. Caching strategy
5. CDN for global content delivery
6. Expiration cleanup mechanism
7. Syntax highlighting implementation
8. Version control for edits
9. Access control (private/public)
10. Capacity planning
11. Scalability approach
questions.realWorldScenario: Building content sharing service with scale requirements

questions.title: Design Twitter Timeline
questions.question:
Design Twitter's home timeline feature.

Requirements:
- 500M users, 200M daily active users
- Users follow average 200 people
- Post a tweet (text, images, videos)
- View home timeline (tweets from followed users)
- Timeline ranking (chronological + algorithmic)
- Real-time tweet appearance (<5 seconds)
- Engagement: like, retweet, reply
- Pagination and infinite scroll
- Mobile and web clients

Design:
1. Database schema (users, tweets, followers)
2. Fan-out on write vs fan-out on read
3. Timeline generation algorithm
4. Caching strategy for timelines
5. Ranking algorithm integration
6. Real-time updates mechanism
7. Media storage and delivery (CDN)
8. Handling celebrity users (high followers)
9. Scalability (database sharding)
10. Performance optimization
11. Capacity estimation
questions.realWorldScenario: Building real-time social media timeline with massive scale

questions.title: Design Instagram Photo Feed
questions.question:
Design Instagram's photo feed and storage system.

Requirements:
- 1B users, 500M daily active users
- Upload photos (up to 10MB)
- View personalized feed
- Like, comment on photos
- Follow users
- Image processing (resize, compress, filters)
- Global CDN delivery
- Mobile-first (95% mobile traffic)

Design:
1. Photo upload flow and processing pipeline
2. Image storage solution (object storage)
3. Multiple resolutions generation
4. CDN strategy for global delivery
5. Database schema
6. Feed generation (fan-out)
7. Personalized ranking algorithm
8. Caching strategy
9. Scalability approach
10. Capacity estimation (storage, bandwidth)
questions.realWorldScenario: Building image-heavy social media platform at scale

questions.title: Design WhatsApp Messaging
questions.question:
Design WhatsApp's one-to-one messaging system.

Requirements:
- 2B users, 1B daily active users
- Send/receive messages in real-time
- Online/offline status
- Message delivery status (sent, delivered, read)
- End-to-end encryption
- Message history storage
- Support text, images, videos, files
- Mobile-first architecture
- Offline message queue

Design:
1. Real-time messaging architecture (WebSocket)
2. Message delivery guarantees
3. Message storage (database design)
4. Encryption implementation
5. Online status tracking
6. Read receipts mechanism
7. Media handling and storage
8. Offline message handling
9. Scalability (connection management)
10. Push notifications
11. Multi-device sync
questions.realWorldScenario: Building real-time messaging with billions of users

questions.title: Design YouTube Video Streaming

3. Storage solution (video files, metadata)
4. CDN strategy for video delivery
5. Adaptive bitrate streaming (HLS/DASH)
6. Database schema
7. Recommendation system integration
8. Search indexing
9. View counter implementation
10. Scalability and cost optimization

questions.title: Design Uber Ride Matching
questions.question:
Design Uber's ride matching system.

Requirements:
- 100M users, 10M drivers
- Real-time driver location updates (every 4 seconds)
- Match rider with nearby driver (<30 seconds)
- ETA calculation
- Dynamic pricing (surge)
- Trip tracking
- Payment processing
- Multi-region deployment

Design:
1. Location tracking architecture
2. Geospatial indexing (quad-tree, geo-hash)
3. Matching algorithm
4. ETA calculation
5. Database schema
6. Real-time updates (WebSocket)
7. Surge pricing calculation
8. Payment integration
9. Trip state management
10. Scalability (sharding by region)
11. High availability design

questions.title: Design Netflix Recommendation System
questions.question:
Design Netflix's recommendation engine.

Requirements:
- 200M subscribers
- Personalized recommendations
- Based on: watch history, ratings, viewing patterns
- Real-time updates
- Cold start problem (new users)
- Trending content
- Multiple recommendation types (home, category, search)
- Performance: recommendations in <200ms

Design:
1. Data collection pipeline
2. ML model architecture (collaborative filtering)
3. Feature engineering
4. Model training infrastructure
5. Real-time serving layer
6. Caching strategy
7. Cold start handling
8. A/B testing framework
9. Database design
10. Scalability approach
11. Monitoring and metrics
